description: Every modeled parameter in Solvency. NONE of these are measurements. Each carries provenance and is overridable in the calculator.

light.label: Light
light.examples: bug fix, small refactor, single-file change
light.provenance: digitalapplied, 'AI Coding Agent Cost Calculator: 10 Tools Compared 2026'
light.provenance_note: The source explicitly states these are modeling assumptions, not industry-standard benchmarks, and that real consumption varies with codebase size, context strategy, and tool configuration. Solvency inherits that caveat verbatim.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.provenance: digitalapplied, 'AI Coding Agent Cost Calculator: 10 Tools Compared 2026'

heavy.label: Heavy
heavy.provenance: digitalapplied, 'AI Coding Agent Cost Calculator: 10 Tools Compared 2026'
heavy.provenance_note: Per-loop token figures for the heavy tier were supplied in the Solvency brief citing the same source. Loop range 20-30 verified against the source.

frontier_efficiency.description: Frontier models are assumed to need fewer agent loops than small models to reach the same result, most visibly on heavy tasks.
frontier_efficiency.provenance: Solvency house assumption. NOT MEASURED and NOT sourced from any published study.
frontier_efficiency.provenance_note: SUPERSEDED WHERE OBSERVED COST OR COMPLETE SOURCE USAGE EXISTS. Artificial Analysis publishes an observed per-task cost for current models; OpenBench publishes complete proxy-measured token usage for the admitted harness slice. Both bypass the loop model and this multiplier entirely, so no efficiency assumption touches them. This multiplier applies ONLY as a labelled fallback for models with a pass rate but neither observed cost nor complete source usage (currently the SEAL and Aider rows). It remains a house assumption with no published source and materially advantages frontier models on the heavy tier. Set to 1.0 to see unadjusted results. Phase 3 replaces the fallback outright.

retry_model.provenance: Solvency house assumption, per the Solvency brief.
retry_model.provenance_note: max_attempts caps expected attempts because in practice an operator abandons or takes over after a few failures. residual_human_cost_usd defaults to $0 so the published headline never silently imputes a labour rate; set it to a real blended hourly cost to model takeover.

cache_hit_fraction.provenance_note: Defaults to 0 (no prompt caching) because caching behaviour is harness-specific and assuming it would understate real-world cost. Providers with no published cached rate cannot be modelled with caching at all.

metr_caveat.text: METR randomized controlled trial: experienced open-source developers took 19% LONGER to complete tasks when using early-2025 AI tools. They expected AI to speed them up by 24%, and even after experiencing the slowdown still believed AI had sped them up by 20%. Solvency measures cost per benchmark-solved task. It does not measure developer throughput, and a low cost-per-solved-task must not be read as a productivity gain.

loop_model_scope.text: The task-tier loop model applies ONLY to rows with cost_basis=modelled_by_solvency. Rows with cost_basis=measured_by_source carry a cost the benchmark source actually observed. Rows with cost_basis=source_usage_repriced carry complete token usage observed by a source and apply current verified model prices. No loop count, per-loop token figure, cache-hit control or frontier-efficiency multiplier is applied to either observed-data basis. All bases are labelled separately and are never averaged together; source-usage-repriced rows are additionally isolated within the same model and benchmark.
